reason: The passage depicts Moses and Aaron actively taking leadership and fulfilling their role as leaders of the Hebrew people. They are called by Pharaoh and deliver God's commandments to the Israelites. The text explicitly states that 'the children of Israel did according to Moses's word' (וּבְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עָשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה) and later reiterates that 'all the children of Israel did as YHWH commanded Moses and Aaron.' Rather than avoiding accountability, they exercise direct leadership that results in the liberation of the people. The passage presents them as faithful instruments executing their leadership responsibilities to free the Hebrew people from Egypt.
